criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.
Given a support request, when it is pasted into the assistant, then it should be classified into a predefined category.
Given a support request, when it is classified, then the assistant should determine its priority.
Trust: The classification and priority determination should be logged in the audit trail.
Given a classified support request, when I review it, then I can approve or reject the classification and priority.
Given a misclassified support request, when I reject it, then it is sent back for reclassification.
Trust: Every approval or rejection action is logged in the audit trail.
Given an action on a support request, when it occurs, then it is logged in the audit trail.
Given a failed logging attempt, when it occurs, then an alert is generated.
Trust: The audit trail is immutable and records all actions accurately.
Given a classified request, when the assistant searches the knowledge base, then it should return relevant troubleshooting steps.
Given a search, when no relevant steps are found, then the assistant should indicate uncertainty.
Trust: The search query and results should be logged in the audit trail.
Given troubleshooting steps, when the assistant generates a response, then it should be professional and based on available information.
Given a response draft, when I review it, then I should be able to edit it before sending.
Trust: The draft generation should be logged in the audit trail.
Given an unresolved issue, when the assistant recommends escalation, then it should provide a clear explanation.
Given an escalation recommendation, when I review it, then I should be able to approve or reject it.
Trust: The escalation recommendation and decision should be logged in the audit trail.
Given a completed workflow, when the assistant generates a support summary, then it should include all relevant details.
Given a support summary, when I review it, then I should be able to save it manually.
Trust: The summary generation should be logged in the audit trail.
Given a rejected classification with a correct category supplied, when the correction is recorded, then it is saved with the keyword, wrong category, and correct category.
Given the same keyword -> correct-category pattern recorded 3 separate times, when the corrections are checked, then a suggested_rule_change proposal is added to the existing ticket queue.
Given a suggested_rule_change proposal, when a human approves it, then classify.js uses the new rule for that keyword going forward; when a human rejects it, then nothing about classify.js changes.
Trust: every correction recorded, every suggestion created, and every approve/reject decision on a suggestion is logged in the audit trail.

criteria.text: Given a ticket a human manually solved after a no-match or weak-confidence knowledge base search, when the human proposes a new article, then it is auto-assigned the next available KB id and added to the existing ticket queue as a suggested_kb_article.

Given a suggested_kb_article proposal, when a human approves it, then it is added to knowledgeBase.json as a real, searchable article tagged source: human_approved_correction; when a human rejects it, then knowledgeBase.json is not touched at all.
Trust: every proposal created and every approve/reject decision is logged in the audit trail.

criteria.text: Given an existing approved classification rule, when a human revokes it with a reason, then the rule is marked revoked (never deleted) and classify.js no longer applies it to new requests.
Given a rule that has already been revoked, when a human attempts to revoke it again, then the second attempt is an idempotent no-op, not an error.
Given a classification already produced using a rule before it was revoked, when the rule is later revoked, then that earlier classification result is unaffected.
Trust: every revocation attempt — successful, not-found, or duplicate — is logged in the audit trail.

criteria.text: Given the same keyword -> correct-category pattern recorded 2 separate times with recordedAt timestamps within FAST_REPEAT_WINDOW_DAYS of each other, when the corrections are checked, then a suggested_rule_change proposal is added to the existing ticket queue with triggeredBy: 'fast_repeat'.

Given the same pattern recorded 2 times more than FAST_REPEAT_WINDOW_DAYS apart, when the corrections are checked, then no suggestion is created on that basis alone (the original 3-times-ever trigger from STORY-008 still applies independently).

Given a pattern that satisfies both the original 3-times-ever trigger and the new fast-repeat trigger at once, when the corrections are checked, then the resulting suggestion reports triggeredBy: 'threshold'.

Given a correction with a missing or unparsable recordedAt, when corrections are checked, then it still counts toward the original 3-times-ever trigger but can never contribute to the fast-repeat trigger.

criteria.text: Given a brand-new support ticket being ingested via ingestSupportTicket(), when it is created, then it is classified automatically in the same call and saved with status 'classified' and a real category and priority — no separate manual classify step required.
Given classification unexpectedly fails during ingestion, when the ticket is saved, then it is still saved with status 'unclassified' and classificationError: true set, rather than being lost.

Given a queued ticket with status 'unclassified' or classificationError: true, when classifyQueuedTicket is called on it, then it is classified and updated in place with a real category and priority, with classificationError cleared; given a ticket that is already classified, when classifyQueuedTicket is called on it, then it is left unchanged.
Trust: the classification performed automatically at ingest, and every classification performed by classifyQueuedTicket, is logged in the audit trail.

stories.notes: Implemented and covered by tests/classifyQueuedTicket.test.js (new) and updated tests in tests/ingestSupportTicket.test.js (npm test: 344/344 pass) — see PROGRESS.md for the full account.

criteria.text: Given a brand-new support ticket being ingested via ingestSupportTicket(), when classification succeeds, then the same call also searches the knowledge base and generates a draft response, saving kbSearchResult and draftResponse onto the ticket alongside its category and priority — no separate manual search/draft step required.

Given knowledgeBaseSearch() or generateDraftResponse() unexpectedly fails after a successful classification (during ingestion, or during classifyQueuedTicket's recovery), when the ticket is saved, then it is still saved with its real classification intact and kbSearchFailed/draftGenerationFailed set, rather than being lost or silently treated as if search or draft had succeeded.

Given submitReviewDecision is called with decision.action 'approve' on a ticket with a real classification, then it calls reviewClassification() to record the human's review decision and builds the summary workflow from the ticket's actual category, priority, kbSearchResult, and draftResponse, so a summary is generated, saved, and the ticket is removed from the queue — instead of failing closed with invalid_classification_review as it did before this story.

Given a ticket that predates this feature (classified, but with no kbSearchResult or draftResponse ever recorded on it), when it is approved, then a summary is still generated and saved, honestly noting that no knowledge-base search or draft was recorded, rather than failing closed.

Given submitReviewDecision's reject path successfully reclassifies a ticket, or classifyQueuedTicket successfully (re)classifies one, when the ticket is requeued or updated, then its kbSearchResult and draftResponse are regenerated to match the new classification and overwrite (never merge with) whatever was there before, so neither is ever left mismatched with a superseded category.

Trust: the search+draft step is logged in the audit trail — one combined entry alongside classification at ingestion, a second combined entry for classifyQueuedTicket's recovery step, and folded into the existing reject-path audit entry — never silently un-audited.
